ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In right triangle $ABC$, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, $BC=2\,\text{cm}$, $CD\perp AB$. Point $E$ is taken on $AC$ such that $EC=2\,\text{cm}$. A line through point $E$ and perpendicular to $AC$ intersects the extension of $CD$ at point $F$. If $AE=3\,\text{cm}$, what is the length of $EF$ in centimeters?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
$\because \angle ACB=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore \angle ECF+\angle BCD=90^\circ$\\
$\because CD\perp AB$\\
$\therefore \angle BCD+\angle B=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore \angle ECF=\angle B$\\
In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle FEC$\\
$\because \angle ECF=\angle B$, $EC=BC$, $\angle ACB=\angle FEC=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore \triangle ABC \cong \triangle FCE$ (ASA)\\
$\therefore AC=EF$\\
$\because AC=AE+CE=3+2=5\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore EF=\boxed{5\text{cm}}$

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: $\because \angle ACB=90^\circ$ $\therefore \angle ECF+\angle BCD=90^\circ$ $\because CD\perp AB$ $\therefore \angle BCD+\angle B=90^\circ$ $\therefore \angle ECF=\angle B$ In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle FEC$, $\because \angle ECF=\angle B$, $EC=BC$, $\angle ACB=\angle FEC=90^\circ$ $\therefore \triangle ABC \cong \triangle FCE$ (ASA) $\therefore AC=EF$ $\because AC=AE+CE=3+2=5\text{ cm}$, $\therefore EF=\boxed{5\text{ cm}}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: The diagram shows A, E, and C collinear vertically with E between A and C. Segment EF is drawn horizontally through E, perpendicular to AC, and meets point F to the right. Triangle ABC is right-angled at C, with BC extending from C toward B. Segment CD is drawn from C to D on AB and is perpendicular to AB; the line CD continues through D to F, so F lies on the extension of CD.

Reasoning: Since ∠ACB = 90°, AC is perpendicular to BC. Because E lies on AC and F lies on the extension of CD, the angles ∠ECF and ∠BCD together make a right angle, so ∠ECF + ∠BCD = 90°. Also, CD ⟂ AB, so in triangle BCD, ∠BCD + ∠ABC = 90°. Therefore ∠ECF = ∠ABC.

Now compare triangles ABC and FEC. We have ∠ACB = ∠FEC = 90° because EF ⟂ AC. We also have ∠ABC = ∠ECF from the angle chase, and BC = EC = 2 cm. Therefore triangles ABC and FEC are congruent by ASA/AAS. Under this correspondence, EF corresponds to AC, so EF = AC.

Since AC = AE + EC = 3 + 2 = 5 cm, it follows that EF = 5 cm.

Final answer: 5 cm.
